title: Jesus’ journeys
allSummary: The life of Jesus, c. 6 BC to AD 30. Tap a chip to follow one phase, use the step buttons to walk through it, or tap any place for what happened there and where to read it. Dates are scholarly estimates and routes are approximate.

0.name: Birth & childhood
0.sum: Birth and childhood, c. 6 BC to AD 8. Born in Bethlehem, presented in the temple, taken to Egypt to escape Herod, and raised in Nazareth. Matthew 1–2; Luke 1–2

1.name: Baptism & early ministry
1.sum: Baptism and early ministry, c. AD 26–27. Baptized by John, tested in the wilderness, then a first sign at Cana, the first Passover in Jerusalem and the conversation at the well in Samaria. Matthew 3–4; John 1–4

2.name: Galilee ministry
2.sum: The Galilee ministry, c. AD 27–29. Capernaum becomes his base. Jesus teaches on the hillside, heals, raises the widow’s son at Nain, is rejected at Nazareth and calms the storm. Matthew 4–13; Mark 1–6; Luke 4–9

3.name: Retreats north & east
3.sum: Retreats beyond Galilee, c. AD 29. Jesus withdraws to the region of Tyre and Sidon and the Decapolis, then north to Caesarea Philippi, where Peter confesses him as the Christ. The transfiguration follows. Mark 7–9; Matthew 15–17

4.name: Road to Jerusalem
4.sum: The road to Jerusalem, c. AD 29–30. Jesus sets his face toward Jerusalem, teaches at the feasts, raises Lazarus at Bethany, withdraws to Ephraim and passes through Jericho. Luke 9:51–19:28; John 7–11

5.name: Passion week
5.sum: Passion week, c. AD 30 (some scholars date it AD 33). The entry into Jerusalem, teaching in the temple, the last supper, Gethsemane, the trials, the cross and the burial. Matthew 21–27; John 12–19

6.name: After the resurrection
6.sum: After the resurrection, forty days. The empty tomb, the road to Emmaus, appearances in Jerusalem and Galilee, and the ascension. Luke 24; John 20–21; Acts 1

0: Jesus is born here during the census. Shepherds hear the angels’ announcement, and later wise men from the east bring gifts. Herod orders the killing of the boys of Bethlehem.

egypt.m: Egypt (traditional route towards the Nile delta)

0: Warned in a dream, Joseph takes Mary and the child to Egypt until Herod dies. They then return and settle in Nazareth.
Jesus grows up here in wisdom and stature, in a family of modest means.
2: Jesus reads from Isaiah in the synagogue and says it is fulfilled. The hometown crowd turns against him and tries to throw him off the hill; he walks away. He does few miracles here because of their unbelief.

0: Presented at the temple, where Simeon and Anna recognise him. At twelve, Jesus stays behind and is found among the teachers: “I must be in my Father’s house.”
1: At the first Passover of his ministry Jesus drives the traders from the temple. By night, Nicodemus comes to him and hears of new birth.
4: Jesus teaches at the Feast of Tabernacles, heals the man born blind, tells of the good shepherd, and speaks at the Feast of Dedication.
5: The triumphal entry, the cleansing of the temple, debates with the leaders, the last supper in an upper room, the arrest, and the trials before the Sanhedrin and Pilate.
6: On the evening of the resurrection and a week later, Jesus appears to the disciples behind locked doors. Thomas sees the wounds and believes.

1: John baptizes Jesus. The Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice from heaven declares him the beloved Son. John points to him as the Lamb of God.
4: Late in his ministry Jesus withdraws across the Jordan to where John had baptized. Many come to him there and believe.

1: After the baptism Jesus fasts forty days and is tempted three times. He answers each temptation from Scripture.
At a wedding, Jesus turns water into wine: the first of his signs.
2: From Cana, Jesus heals a royal official’s son at Capernaum with a word.

1: Tired from the journey, Jesus talks with a Samaritan woman at Jacob’s well and tells her of living water. Many Samaritans of the town believe.

2: Jesus’ base in Galilee. He calls Peter, Andrew, James and John, heals Peter’s mother-in-law, forgives and heals a paralysed man let down through the roof, and heals the centurion’s servant.
Jesus teaches the Sermon on the Mount, beginning with the Beatitudes. The exact hill is unknown; this traditional site overlooks the lake.
Jesus meets a funeral procession and raises a widow’s only son, moved with compassion for her.
After calming the storm on the lake, Jesus lands here and frees a man from a legion of unclean spirits. The people ask him to leave, and the healed man tells his story across the Decapolis.
3: Jesus passes back through the region of the Decapolis, heals a deaf man, and feeds the four thousand.
Near here Jesus feeds the five thousand with five loaves and two fish. At Bethsaida he also heals a blind man in two stages.
In the region of Tyre and Sidon Jesus meets a Syrophoenician woman. Moved by her faith, he heals her daughter.
Jesus passes through Sidon on the way back to the Sea of Galilee and the Decapolis.
Jesus asks, “Who do you say that I am?” Peter answers that he is the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus begins to speak openly of his suffering, death and resurrection.

transfiguration.m: Mount Tabor (traditional); Mount Hermon also proposed

3: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James and John. Moses and Elijah appear, and the Father’s voice says, “Listen to him.” The Gospels name no mountain; tradition says Tabor, and some suggest Hermon.

4: After raising Lazarus, and with the leaders plotting against him, Jesus withdraws with his disciples to a town called Ephraim.
On the final approach to Jerusalem, Jesus heals blind Bartimaeus and visits Zacchaeus, the chief tax collector, who gives back what he took.
Jesus raises Lazarus, four days dead, after telling Martha, “I am the resurrection and the life.”
5: Six days before the Passover, Mary anoints Jesus at a dinner here. Jesus stays in Bethany each night of the week.
Jesus weeps over Jerusalem, then teaches his disciples about the end of the age on the Mount of Olives.
6: Forty days after the resurrection, Jesus is taken up from the mountain called Olivet. Two men in white say he will return in the same way.

5: Jesus prays in agony, “Not my will, but yours.” Judas arrives with the crowd, and Jesus is arrested.

golgotha.m: Church of the Holy Sepulchre area, Jerusalem

5: Jesus is crucified at the place of the Skull and buried in a nearby new tomb.
6: Early on the first day of the week the tomb is empty. Jesus appears first to Mary Magdalene.

emmaus.m: site disputed (Qubeibeh, Abu Ghosh and others)

6: On the evening of the resurrection, Jesus walks with two disciples who do not recognise him, explains the Scriptures, and is known to them in the breaking of bread.

tabgha.n: Shore of the Sea of Galilee

6: Jesus appears to seven disciples after a night of fishing and cooks breakfast on the shore. He restores Peter: “Feed my sheep.” He also meets the eleven on a mountain in Galilee and sends them to all nations.
